evidence.claim: AI infrastructure demand is pressuring advanced packaging, power, and optical interconnect supply chains, creating a need to look beyond GPUs into physical bottlenecks.
evidence.source_title: Cached Layer 2 Serenity evidence: AI buildouts hit three bottlenecks at once in April 2026

evidence.claim: Optical interconnects, 800G, 1.6T, CPO, silicon photonics, photonics components, and optical EMS/test capacity were identified in Layer 2 as relevant AI infrastructure nodes.

Layer 2 included a hypothesis that EMS and optical-manufacturing earnings disclosing datacom growth, customer concentration, capacity additions, and 800G/1.6T yield improvements can surface underfollowed bottleneck beneficiaries hidden inside broad manufacturing labels.
Layer 2 included a hypothesis that named hyperscaler design wins or volume orders for 800G and 1.6T optical modules can confirm that optical interconnect scarcity is moving from narrative to revenue.

A supplied May 2026 source says the AI-server MLCC bottleneck is concentrated in high-end parts that combine small size, high capacitance, low ESR, and low ESL, with only a few companies able to mass-produce them.
evidence.source_title: Murata: The Stock You Missed If You Only Bought GPUs and HBM in the AI Rally

evidence.claim: External search context frames the Serenity chokepoint approach as focused on concentrated, irreplaceable, qualification-gated, and underdiscovered suppliers, especially where volume-ramp inflection produces revenue acceleration and margin improvement.

External search context identifies Broadcom Q2 FY2026 semiconductor revenue growth as driven by custom AI accelerators and AI networking, making Broadcom a demand reference for the custom silicon and networking lane.
evidence.source_title: Signals from SEC Filings — Tech Supply Chain

memory_update.content: For AI optical-interconnect candidate chunks, prioritize companies with direct evidence of 800G/1.6T datacenter revenue, qualified manufacturing/test capacity, customer concentration that can be monitored, and margin behavior showing scarcity rather than cyclical telecom recovery.

Fabrinet should remain the top underfollowed optical EMS candidate until falsified by weak datacom mix, lack of 800G/1.6T commentary, customer insourcing, margin compression, or capacity/yield problems.

Use Broadcom, Lumentum, and Coherent primarily as demand and component-scarcity reference leaders; avoid allowing their popularity or market capitalization to crowd out underfollowed EMS, test, and manufacturing candidates.

For AAOI, Sanmina, Jabil, Celestica, and Aeluma, the next layer must verify whether AI/datacenter optical exposure is material, durable, margin-accretive, and backed by customer orders or production programs.

ranked_candidates.hidden_signal_to_verify: Check latest 10-K/10-Q customer concentration, datacom versus telecom mix, 800G/1.6T commentary, Thailand capacity additions, inventory/yield language, gross margin behavior, and whether any large customer is insourcing assembly.
ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: Need direct confirmation that AI datacenter 800G/1.6T programs, not legacy telecom or non-AI optical demand, are driving revenue growth, capacity utilization, and margin resilience.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: Fabrinet has the cleanest Serenity-style combination in this chunk: durable AI datacenter bandwidth demand, a real bottleneck candidate in qualified optical manufacturing and testing, visible public-market exposure, and a concrete evidence path through customer concentration, datacom mix, capacity, yield, and margin behavior.
ranked_candidates.why_underfollowed: It is often screened as contract manufacturing or optical communications services rather than as a core AI interconnect scaling bottleneck behind module, networking, and hyperscaler ecosystem customers.

ranked_candidates.hidden_signal_to_verify: Verify cloud/networking product growth, AI datacenter revenue mix, order duration, capacity constraints, customer concentration, and whether margins show scarcity rather than cyclical telecom recovery.
ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: Need product-level and customer-level evidence that cloud/AI datacenter optics, rather than telecom rebound or inventory normalization, is the main driver.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: Lumentum is a strong reference candidate for AI photonics scarcity because it maps directly to lasers and optical components used in high-speed datacenter interconnects. It is less underfollowed than Fabrinet but remains useful for checking whether cloud/AI demand is tightening component-level supply.
ranked_candidates.why_underfollowed: It can be misread as a legacy telecom or broad optical component supplier even when the relevant signal is constrained cloud and AI datacenter optics capacity.

ranked_candidates.hidden_signal_to_verify: Check whether AI datacenter optics, not telecom or industrial demand, is driving backlog, capacity additions, gross margin, capex, and mix improvement.
ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: Need separation of AI/datacenter optics contribution from industrial, telecom, and other photonics end markets.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: Coherent is a high-quality reference leader for compound-semiconductor and photonics capacity tied to AI optical scaling. It scores well on bottleneck severity and supplier scarcity, but the company is broad enough that public-market purity and falsifiability are weaker than Fabrinet or Lumentum.
ranked_candidates.why_underfollowed: Often categorized as a broad photonics, industrial laser, or compound semiconductor company, which can obscure the AI datacenter optical-capacity angle.

ranked_candidates.hidden_signal_to_verify: Confirm order size, shipment timing, margin profile, customer concentration, manufacturing capacity, yields, and whether 800G revenue can scale beyond one hyperscaler customer.
ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: Need proof that 800G orders are durable, profitable, and diversified rather than a one-customer or one-cycle demand spike.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: AAOI has high upside as a testable underfollowed optical-module candidate if qualified 800G revenue scales beyond a narrow customer base. It ranks below the larger photonics leaders because the evidence quality and risk clarity are weaker, but its public-market purity and hidden-signal value are high.
ranked_candidates.why_underfollowed: It may be categorized as a volatile optical/telecom component company rather than an AI datacenter interconnect manufacturing beneficiary.

ranked_candidates.hidden_signal_to_verify: Determine whether photonics is financially material: segment revenue, named customers, 800G/1.6T design wins, gross-margin contribution, and whether the Intel silicon-photonics asset acquisition is converting into AI datacenter production revenue.
ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: Need evidence that photonics or silicon-photonics manufacturing is material enough to move consolidated revenue and margins.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: Jabil is an attractive second-order underfollowed candidate if photonics and silicon-photonics manufacturing become scaling gates for AI datacenter optics. It scores well on discovery and testability, but lower on purity because AI optics may be financially diluted inside diversified EMS operations.
ranked_candidates.why_underfollowed: Jabil is widely known as a diversified EMS company, so AI optical interconnect exposure can be diluted inside broader manufacturing, server, packaging, supply-chain, and industrial revenue categories.

ranked_candidates.hidden_signal_to_verify: Verify management commentary, AI server MLCC revenue contribution, capacity utilization, high-end MLCC pricing, customer mix, and whether demand is incremental versus substitution from smartphones or automotive.
ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: Need explicit evidence that AI-server MLCC demand is large enough to affect mix, pricing, utilization, or margins.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: Murata is a differentiated non-optics chokepoint candidate because AI servers and racks may increase high-end MLCC intensity. It ranks below the optical names because the evidence path is less direct and AI exposure may be diluted by smartphones, automotive, and broader electronics cycles.
ranked_candidates.why_underfollowed: AI screens often emphasize GPUs, HBM, networking, and power equipment while missing the per-server and per-rack passive component intensity embedded in AI hardware BOMs.

ranked_candidates.hidden_signal_to_verify: Verify AI/datacenter customer mix, cloud and communications revenue, networking platform exposure, optical or switch-related manufacturing content, gross-margin contribution, backlog durability, and customer concentration.
ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: The supplied candidate record is truncated, so the exact AI optical-interconnect or bottleneck linkage needs primary-source verification.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: Celestica remains relevant as a potential AI datacenter, networking, and manufacturing beneficiary, but the provided chunk gives less complete evidence than for Fabrinet, Lumentum, Coherent, AAOI, or Jabil. It should survive Layer 3 only as a candidate requiring sharper mapping to optical, switch, or AI infrastructure manufacturing bottlenecks.
ranked_candidates.why_underfollowed: It can be screened as a diversified EMS and hardware-platform company rather than as a beneficiary of AI datacenter networking and manufacturing complexity.

ranked_candidates.hidden_signal_to_verify: Review latest 10-K/10-Q segment commentary, earnings-call transcripts, customer concentration disclosures, optical facility materials, and capex language for datacenter optics or high-speed networking acceleration.
ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: Need confirmation that datacenter optics or high-speed networking is financially material, not just a capability listed in company materials.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: Sanmina is a classic Serenity shadow candidate: potentially exposed to qualified optical, RF, microelectronics, and test manufacturing, but hidden inside a diversified EMS label. It ranks below Jabil because current evidence quality is weaker and AI datacenter optics materiality is not yet established.
ranked_candidates.why_underfollowed: The company is usually screened as a diversified EMS or industrial manufacturing name rather than an AI optical-interconnect bottleneck supplier.

ranked_candidates.hidden_signal_to_verify: Validate latest SEC filings and earnings materials for AI semiconductor revenue, hyperscaler customer concentration, custom ASIC pipeline, networking growth, backlog durability, and whether revenue is pull-forward.
ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: Need to separate durable custom AI accelerator/networking demand from pull-forward, customer concentration, and capacity-timing effects.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: Broadcom is not an underfollowed discovery, but it remains an important reference leader for validating custom AI silicon and AI networking demand. It should be used as a demand read-through for the optical, packaging, substrate, and manufacturing candidates rather than as the main Serenity alpha target in this chunk.
ranked_candidates.why_underfollowed: Not underfollowed overall, but useful as a reference leader for checking whether value is migrating from GPU-centric training to hyperscaler-specific inference silicon and networking supply chains.

ranked_candidates.hidden_signal_to_verify: Look for named AI/datacenter customers, production purchase orders, qualified foundry/manufacturing partners, product-level datacom photodetector specifications, cash runway, and revenue contribution from optical interconnect applications.
ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: Need proof of commercial traction in AI/datacenter optical interconnects, including production orders, qualified partners, and revenue contribution.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: Aeluma has high theoretical Serenity fit as a speculative shadow candidate: if InP or photodetector capacity becomes a binding constraint, a scalable III-V-on-silicon platform could matter. However, evidence quality is currently too weak for high research priority beyond a speculative watchlist.
ranked_candidates.why_underfollowed: It is a small-cap, early-stage platform company that may be screened as sensors or compound semiconductors rather than AI optical interconnect manufacturing.

summary: This Layer 3 ranking prioritizes candidates closest to AI optical-interconnect, photonics-component, precision-manufacturing, and board-level component chokepoints. Fabrinet ranks first because it combines durable AI bandwidth demand, qualified precision manufacturing, customer/yield bottleneck characteristics, and a relatively underappreciated AI-infrastructure framing. Lumentum and Coherent are stronger reference leaders for photonics scarcity but have somewhat lower underfollowed scores. AAOI, Jabil, Sanmina, Celestica, and Aeluma remain evidence-sensitive underfollowed or speculative paths where the key test is whether AI datacenter optics revenue is real, scalable, margin-accretive, and not merely cyclical telecom recovery. Broadcom is retained only as a reference demand validator, not an underfollowed discovery.
